newsitem.title: USA: US Commerce Dpt encryption export rules out soon.
newsitem.headline: US Commerce Dpt encryption export rules out soon.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Commerce, working to complete rules implementing a new encryption export policy, will begin consulting with affected parties as early as Wednesday, an administration official said.

"We are nearly finished drafting the regulation," under secretary of Commerce William Reinsch said at a briefing here. "We hope to begin the consultation process with members of industry tomorrow. If we don't quite make that, it will have to kick over to Monday."

Under an executive order signed by President Bill Clinton Nov. 15, export restrictions will be relaxed on encryption technology -- computer programs that scramble information so it cannot be read without a password or software "key."
Encryption has become widely used, for example to safeguard a company's electronic mail messages or to keep credit card numbers transmitted over the Internet away from criminals.

Currently, U.S. companies are prohibited from exporting products with strong encryption. Under the new policy, companies could export strong products if the products also had a feature known as "key recovery," which allows the government easily to break the coding.

Also, companies could export slightly stronger encryption immediately if they committed to incorporating key recovery features within two years. Use of encryption within the United States remains unrestricted.
But no company can take advantage of the new policy until the Commerce Department promulgates rules spelling out details such as what will qualify as a "key escrow" enabled feature.
Reinsch, speaking at a briefing sponsored by the House Science Committee's Subcommittee on Technology, said his office is "on track" to issue the final rules on January 1, 1997.
Several companies, including International Business Machines Corp and Hewlett-Packard Co, have said they will have products on the market soon that will meet the government's to-be-announced rules.
